quotes.text: The cure for password sprawl isn't to hide the passwords better, it's to replace them with something that self destructs when it's misused.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sums up the core argument of the episode: eliminate secrets instead of hiding them.

quotes.text: Passwords are static. Tokens are temporary and scoped, which means if they leak, the blast radius is tiny and the clock is already ticking before they expire.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear, memorable contrast between passwords and tokens.

quotes.text: Those consent prompts are your audit trail. They tell you what the app is asking for and who approved it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes consent prompts from annoyance to a security control.

quotes.text: OBO is less about extra work and more about keeping the chain of trust unbroken from front end to back end, all the way down to the database.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the purpose of the On-Behalf-Of flow in one sentence.

quotes.text: Security isn't always about more tools, it's about using the ones you already have properly.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A practical recommendation that applies beyond Azure identity.

takeaways: Hard-coded secrets spread across configs, repos and backups, so the fix is to stop using them rather than hide them better.
Entra ID issues short-lived, scoped access tokens, and managed identities let Azure resources obtain them without any stored credentials.
Careful app registrations, claims checks in your APIs and the On-Behalf-Of flow keep permissions tight and the chain of trust intact across services.
hook: Still hiding passwords and connection strings in config files, Key Vault or Git history? This episode is for Azure developers and admins who want to replace secrets with Entra ID tokens and managed identities. You will learn how app registrations, claims checks and the On-Behalf-Of flow keep real-world apps secure without credential sprawl.
